nodes.question: Is the same DVD item that appears as the small rectangular case/package near the center of SOURCE visibly white in EDITED?
nodes.criteria: Compare the small rectangular item near the center of SOURCE with EDITED. Pass only if that same item can be reliably matched in EDITED and its visible body/surface is predominantly white; fail if the matched item remains non-white or black; unknown if the source item cannot be reliably located or matched in EDITED, or its color cannot be judged. Do not count the dark object at right in SOURCE or newly visible discs as the target without establishing correspondence.
nodes.binding: The target is the small rectangular DVD item near the center of SOURCE, not another object or a newly appearing disc unless it can be reliably identified as that same item.

nodes.necessity: The instruction requests changing the black DVD to white. program.decomposition_reason: Only one distinct visual dimension is justified: the DVD’s color. Retaining DVD identity is stated in the outcome description, but the instruction itself requests a color transformation and does not make identity retention a separate visual change to assess. Splitting the color change into multiple checks would duplicate the same endpoint.

d1: The binding appears to misidentify the target: the small rectangular item near the center of SOURCE looks like a DVD case/package, while the instruction’s “black DVD” may refer to the dark disc-like object at right. The edited image shows a white disc at that right-hand location, which is plausible evidence of progress, but the other white disc is not evidence by itself. Revisit target identity using shape, position, and scene correspondence rather than treating the rectangular item as certain; keep the match requirement explicit and allow unresolved when correspondence is genuinely unclear. The traces’ repeated high-confidence unknown/fail split reflects this binding ambiguity, not a transport or dependency failure. Avoid converting mere absence of the rectangular case into a definite fail unless the criterion establishes that it is the instructed DVD; likewise, do not infer completion solely from a white-looking disc without reliable identity.
